html:
The arrival in Southeast Asia of the first cholera pandemic, which had broken out in Bengal in 1817. In 1820 and 1821 it killed tens of thousands in Bangkok and on Java.

The pandemic travelled by ship along trade routes from the Bay of Bengal. In Bangkok, capital of the young Rattanakosin Kingdom, the dead were too many to cremate in the usual way, and the king ordered Buddhist ceremonies to drive out the sickness. In Java the disease spread from Batavia along the north coast and into the interior. In Manila in 1820, crowds who blamed foreigners for poisoning the water killed a number of them.

Nobody knew the cause, and cholera came back to the region again and again during the 19th century. The next wave of the disease would carry it much further, as cholera reached Europe in 1830.
